cards.title: Typed symbols
cards.text: Latitude phi, longitude lambda, planar orientation theta, unwrapped phase Phi, symbolic pi, prime integers, and prime marks have different typed meanings. Pi is stored symbolically with an exact rational coefficient.

cards.title: Integer angle lattice
cards.text: Angles count nanodegrees: 360000000000 ticks per turn. Theta is an unsigned 39-bit word below one turn. Latitude and longitude use signed 40-bit words with separate geographic domains. Off-grid input and nonperiodic overflow require explicit handling.

cards.title: Frames and height
cards.text: Latitude, heading, and phase are different coordinates. Heights require ellipsoidal or orthometric meaning, datum, and units. Pole longitude and zero-radius orientation have undefined flags. Model-grid resolution does not establish measurement accuracy.

cards.title: Orientation and winding
cards.text: Unwrapped phase is Phi = winding * 360000000000 + theta. The signed 32-bit winding and wrapped theta reconstruct a signed 71-bit phase. Six 60-degree orientation rotations restore orientation; six phase advances add a complete turn.

cards.title: D6 action
cards.text: D6 contains six rotations and six reflections. On wrapped angles, g(theta) = ((1-2*b)*theta + k*60000000000) mod 360000000000, for k in 0..5 and b in 0..1. The structure preserved by an automorphism must be specified.

cards.title: Hexagonal lattice
cards.text: Axial rotation maps (q,r) to (-r,q+r); reflection maps it to (q+r,-r). These preserve q*q+q*r+r*r and the regular hexagonal lattice. Invariance of arbitrary measured fields or learned weights must be established separately.

cards.title: Preserved scalar LUT
cards.text: The source table has 17 radial rows and 72 angular columns, 16-bit codes, and an independent validity mask. The importer reproduced 1158 valid and 66 invalid positions. All 14688 D6 actions preserve these stored codes and mask bits exactly.

cards.title: Finite orbit reduction
cards.text: An independent calculation gives seven angular orbits with representatives 0..6 and sizes 6,12,12,12,12,12,6. The complete grid has 119 orbit representatives, of which 113 are valid. This reduction applies to this invariant fixture; supplied binary files retain the original full representation.

cards.title: Lookup boundaries
cards.text: A masked-out zero is not a valid zero. Check the validity bit before using the signal. The center has its own record. The interval between center and first ring is unrepresented; default addressing selects exact nodes, with no silently introduced interpolation.

cards.title: Exact logarithmic levels
cards.text: The separate exact_log2_levels_64 table maps code k in 0..63 to 2^k-1. Exact encoding accepts only those levels. Floor, ceil, and nearest with ties upward are explicitly lossy policies for values between levels. These codes do not reinterpret Q16 codes.

cards.title: Q16 inverse
cards.text: The Q16 fixture decodes to normalized signal 16^(q/65535)-1. It can be kept symbolic or bounded using integer-power comparisons. The interval covers evaluation of a stored code; sensor uncertainty, initial quantization, clipping, and interpolation remain separate.

cards.title: Reversible transport
cards.text: Whole fields preserve their types and widths when swizzled or interleaved. A coordinate frame contains 217 payload bits followed by seven zero padding bits. Interleaving does not make acquisition times simultaneous. Partial frames are errors.

cards.title: Data origin and uncertainty
cards.text: The embedded bundle consists of generated arithmetic fixtures and a retained synthetic LUT. Calibration and physical uncertainty are null. Exact integer processing and source-code preservation do not imply accurate physical measurements.

cards.title: Units and irreversible loss
cards.text: Logarithm arguments must be dimensionless with declared references. Averaging log codes generally differs from averaging physical signals. An inverse cannot restore discarded data; mixing, clipping, and repeated logarithmic stages need explicit models.

cards.title: Finite memory remains finite
cards.text: A bounded radial display can place every finite radius inside a disk, but a finite raster or buffer cannot retain unlimited spatial precision. Reconstruction grows sensitive near the boundary. A visual projection does not change the physical metric.

cards.title: Actual sensor capabilities
cards.text: Sensor interpretation needs the actual architecture, exposure timing, spectral response, and calibration. A camera should be labeled CCD only if its hardware is CCD. Pixel counts alone cannot establish chemistry, UV conversion, or mechanical properties.

cards.title: Pipeline inspiration
cards.text: The discussion proposes ingestion queues, structured code parsing, positional context, log-polar tables, signal transforms, and edge execution. These themes can inspire an engineered pipeline, but the export does not establish that they are Codex internals or a complete AI architecture.

cards.title: Independent mathematical domains
cards.text: Exponential integrals, bel scaling, Fresnel propagation, log-polar coordinates, and polar channel codes solve different problems. Their shared terminology does not make them one universal transform or demonstrate an implementation on the phone.

cards.title: Radio hardware claims
cards.text: The export discusses satellite, protected navigation, military communications, adaptive antenna arrays, and FPGA baseband processing. These descriptions do not supply compatible hardware, service credentials, or Android APIs, and do not establish those capabilities on a POCO phone.

cards.title: Runtime design boundary
cards.text: The current source packet defines numerical data and operations. It supplies no trained language model, Hugging Face account inventory, general learning rule, or dynamic AI law D(t). A time-indexed state, resource router, model adapter, and JIT are separately specified engineering extensions.

Symbol registry
Letter case, mathematical constants, prime integers and prime marks occupy distinct
namespaces.


 Symbol              Machine meaning

 φ                   latitude_phi_word: geodetic latitude, the ellipsoid-normal angle.

 λ                   longitude_lambda_word: east-positive longitude in its canonical interval.

 h/H                 Ellipsoidal height / orthometric height, with explicit height-kind metadata.

 θ                   theta_word: local planar angle, counterclockwise from local +x.

 Φ                   Phi_unwrapped_word: accumulated local phase with its winding count.

 φc / θc             Geocentric latitude / geocentric colatitude; separate derived coordinates.

 π                   Exact symbolic circle constant; no finite numeric approximation is stored.

 p                   Prime integer: an integer greater than one with exactly two positive divisors.

 π(n)                Prime-counting function; a different object from the circle constant. [U08]

 φ′ or Φ′            An explicitly named transformed value or derivative, according to operator metadata.


Symbolic π without floating-point storage


The packet stores a symbolic basis named pi and an exact rational coefficient. The numerator and
denominator are integer bit strings. For example, 60° has coefficient 1/3 and 5° has coefficient 1/36.
Symbolic Pi and numerical evaluation are separate representations. [U09]

Prime integers are not the circle constant π. The prime-counting function happens to use the letter
π, while a prime mark qualifies an operation. The registry keeps these meanings explicit so a parser
does not infer one from another.

Angle-unit marks are also typed: one arcminute is π/10800 radians; one arcsecond is π/648000 radians. A
mark used as an angular unit is not a derivative operator.

One-bit cells and integer words
A bit has the value 0 or 1. A word assembles multiple bits into a larger exact integer.




The active JSON profiles contain only 0 or 1 as numeric literals. Wider quantities are binary strings or
rational records with binary numerator and denominator. Packed .bin files store the bit cells directly.
Word order is most-significant bit first; signed words use two’s complement.

 Field                              Bits        Range / unit

 Latitude φ                         40 signed   -90,000,000,000 to +90,000,000,000 nanodegrees

 Longitude λ                        40 signed   [-180,000,000,000, +180,000,000,000) nanodegrees

 Local θ                            39          0 through 359,999,999,999 nanodegrees
                                    unsigned

 Height                             64 signed   Integer millimetres; height kind and datum in metadata

 Winding w                          32 signed   -2³¹ through 2³¹-1 complete turns

 Derived Φ ticks                    71 signed   U = wN + j; reconstructed from winding and θ

 Validity / longitude               1 each      Independent boolean bit fields
 defined




Canonical ingestion
Parse decimal-degree text with at most nine fractional digits using integer arithmetic. Thus the text
"52.123456789" becomes the integer 52,123,456,789 ticks. A rational multiple of π is accepted
when its exact coefficient lands on this lattice. The default policy returns a domain error for off-grid
inputs; it does not round silently.

   turn = 360000000000
   theta = raw_theta % turn
   longitude = (raw_lon + turn//2) % turn - turn//2
   winding, theta = divmod(unwrapped_ticks, turn)



The unsigned 39-bit word has unused codes at and above N. Those codes are rejected. Signed overflow
is also rejected; wraparound is used only for explicitly periodic angle operations.

Use the declared reference ellipsoid, coordinate frame and height type.

θ, φ and Φ across frames
Geographic latitude, local orientation and accumulated phase remain distinct.




Geodetic φ measures the ellipsoid normal; geocentric φc measures the Earth-center position vector.
They coincide at the equator and poles. The surface relation tan φc = (1-e²) tan φ applies at h = 0;
use the full ECEF vector for other heights. [U03]

Local east-north convention




Here φ₀ and λ₀ belong to the local origin; ΔX, ΔY and ΔZ are point-minus-origin ECEF differences. The
heading formula converts a clockwise bearing from north to the counterclockwise angle from east.
Record the origin, axes and CRS. At zero planar radius, orientation has an independent undefined flag. A
polar local frame needs an explicit reference direction. [U06]

Unwrapped uppercase Φ


Euclidean division gives 0 ≤ j < N even for negative U. The packet transmits the 32-bit winding and
39-bit wrapped angle, from which the 71-bit signed phase is recovered. Adding one full turn
changes U by N and w by one, while leaving wrapped θ unchanged.

log net D                                                                            UNIVERSAL




Q16 inverse with integer bounds
The original logarithmic inverse can be carried symbolically or evaluated into a certified rational
interval.




The exact expression is stored as a typed syntax tree. For a numerical result without floating-point
arithmetic, choose a positive integer output scale S and reduce q/65535 to p/d using the greatest
common divisor.




If nᵈ = A, both endpoints collapse to the exact rational value. Otherwise the interval width is 1/S.
The guarantee follows from monotonicity of the positive d-th power; every comparison is between
integers.

     g = gcd(q, 65535)
     p, d = q//g, 65535//g
     A = (S ** d) << (4*p)
     lo, hi = S, 16*S + 1
     while hi - lo > 1:
         mid = (lo + hi)//2
         if mid**d <= A: lo = mid
         else: hi = mid
     lower = (lo-S, S) # exact numerator/denominator




 Code                      Exact normalized result

 0                         0

 21,845                    16^(1/3) - 1

 43,690                    16^(2/3) - 1

 65,535                    15


The bundle includes q16_integer_interval.py and its checks. Larger S narrows the output interval and
increases integer computation. The interval describes evaluation of the stored code; acquisition
uncertainty and the original code quantization remain separate quantities.

Use a unit-consistent encoder and its exact analytic inverse.

The scalar signal encoder and the spatial coordinate transform have separate definitions.

                                                            sufficient SNR.

                                                            and crosstalk control. [M14]

    C0 / 0           C1 / 0          C2 / 0        C3 / 0     C0 / 1         C1 / 1         C2 / 1        C3 / 1



The slots above show two frames with four channels each. This digital layout does not imply that the four
measurements were made simultaneously.

A sequential analog scanner has time offsets


Example: 1,000 conversions/s shared uniformly by four channels gives 250 samples/s per channel
and offsets of 0, 1, 2 and 3 ms within a frame. The nominal per-channel Nyquist frequency is 125
Hz; practical filtering and settling need margin. Preserve exposure intervals as well as sample
timestamps. [M03]

Separating mixed measurements requires sufficient independent channels, a calibrated matrix A and
acceptable conditioning. Nonlinear log encoding generally does not commute with mixing: each
logarithm needs its declared positive, dimensionless argument. A broadband CCD count integrates
spectral contributions; an RGB swizzle cannot recover arbitrary unmeasured wavelengths. Follow the
actual acquisition order when demixing, calibrating and encoding. [M01,M14]

log net D                                                           PHYSICAL AND ELECTRONIC INTERFACE




CCD: photons to measured records
Specify the actual sensor, its spectral path and its timing architecture.


A CCD collects photo-generated charge and transfers charge packets toward an output node. The
readout converts charge to voltage; conditioning and an ADC then produce digital counts.
Correlated double sampling can reduce reset-related noise. Sensor saturation, dark signal, read
noise and nonuniform response constrain interpretation. [M01]




The integral gives the expected collected signal-electron count, excluding dark signal and readout
effects. Eλ is sensor-plane irradiance in W·m⁻²·m⁻¹, λ is in metres, pixel area Aₚ is in m², and QE is
electrons per incident photon. Photon energy is hc/λ. Relating specimen illumination to sensor-plane Eλ
needs optical throughput; noise, spatial averaging and transfer losses require additional terms.

An explicit calibration model



 Symbol              Declared meaning

 DN                  Raw digital number for the relevant pixel/exposure.

 B                   Bias/offset map in counts.

 D                   Dark-signal rate in counts per second.

 tₑ                  Exposure duration in seconds.

 F                   Dimensionless normalized flat-field response.


This proposed model yields corrected counts. If a measured dark frame already includes bias, do not
subtract the bias twice. Irradiance or photon-flux units additionally need calibrated gain, spectral
response, optical geometry and exposure time. Match dark and flat measurements to the operating
conditions. [M01]


      Three measurement boundaries
      A pixel count alone does not identify lipid chemistry, UV conversion or mechanical stiffness.
      Sequential readout alone does not establish rolling exposure. Label the device CCD only if its
      specified architecture is CCD; use the camera’s documented shutter and storage timing.

spectral filtering and avoid inferring dose from a display-brightness control. Preserve raw counts
alongside calibration and status metadata.

Analog logarithm and digital code
Each logarithmic stage needs its own reference, scale, domain and inverse.




In this illustrative calibrated analog model, I is a positive current, Iᵣₑf is a positive reference current,
A is an offset voltage, and B is volts per decade. Hardware bandwidth, temperature response, noise
and clipping limits remain part of the measurement.

A concrete component example


Texas Instruments specifies this scale for the LOG114 log-ratio amplifier, with an input-current
range of 100 pA to 10 mA under its stated conditions. Scaling/offset circuitry can match the output
to an ADC. This is an example for a compatible current-monitor channel; it does not establish direct
compatibility with a particular CCD camera output. [M02]

If an analog log stage precedes digitization, first invert its calibrated transfer when estimating the
physical signal. Apply the optional digital encoder only after that interpretation. Recording both
transfers makes a deliberate two-stage encoding reproducible.

Zeros, signed residuals and uncertainty
Bias-corrected estimates can be negative near the noise floor. Keep them for unbiased
measurement analysis, or define a separate signed representation. Silently clipping every negative
estimate to zero changes the estimated mean. A proposed signed display encoder is:

encoder, small code uncertainty propagates approximately as σₛ ≈ L(s+s₀)σᵤ; this is only the encoding

Light, motion and UV exposure
The supplied Fresnel/parabolic diagram concerns collimation; exposure also needs spatial
calibration.


The optics illustration is retained in Appendix A. Parallel output rays describe direction, while curing
depends on the irradiance distribution, wavelength, transmission and time at the specimen. A
collimated beam can still have a nonuniform intensity profile. Appendix A gives the supporting
optics references and source credit.




X labels a material point; c and φ describe specimen translation and rotation; b is beam position; g
is a temporal gate. In this convention p has irradiance units and B is a dimensionless measured
profile. The integral H has radiant-exposure units. Decode logged irradiance before integration.

Planning an exposure field



A proposed dwell-time controller uses Aⱼₖ as calibrated irradiance at target j from exposure position
k. Solve for nonnegative dwell times τₖ under travel, time and uniformity constraints. The point
formula t = H/I is sufficient only for a constant local irradiance with the relevant overlap and motion
already accounted for.

A cure working curve is a fitted material model


The Jacobs working-curve form relates cure depth C_d to exposure using fitted penetration depth Dₚ
and threshold H_c. NIST’s interlaboratory work documents the measurement dependence of these
parameters. Use the fit only within the tested resin, spectrum, geometry and exposure regime.
Equal nominal H need not guarantee equal reaction histories. [M15; Appendix A, A3]

log net D                                                                         BIOCHEMICAL MATERIAL CONCEPT




Preparaat 1 + preparaat 2
Select the chemical roles before choosing the optical or digital control settings.


Preparaat 1: a defined lipid preparation
Specify lipid identity, purity, concentration, hydration and domain structure. Native lipid droplets
may be entrapped within a polymer network; entrapment does not establish covalent bonding to the
carbohydrate. Reactive lipid-derived materials are another route: photocurable acrylated epoxidized
soybean oil is a documented example, not evidence that any oil will UV-harden. [M20]

Preparaat 2: a compatible carbohydrate-derived network
A functionalized polysaccharide can provide reactive groups for network formation. Methacrylated
hyaluronic acid is a published example of a photocrosslinked hydrogel system whose formulation
affects swelling and mechanics. The master does not select a formulation, initiator or dose without
the missing material and wavelength specifications. [M19]


  Architecture                                  Question to resolve


  Lipid domains in a continuous                 Do domains remain stable during mixing and curing, and remain
  network                                       retained after swelling?


  Sequential lipid/carbohydrate                 Does the interface adhere under wet conditions and differential
  layers                                        swelling?


  Reactive lipid + reactive                     Do the selected chemistries actually couple, and what
  carbohydrate                                  independent controls demonstrate this?

 Meaning                                        Required evidence

 Macroscopic hexagonal shape                    Dimensions, imaging and boundary geometry.

 Hexagonal liquid-crystalline lipid             Phase-sensitive scattering with indexed peaks and
 phase                                          composition/temperature context.

Hexagonal mesophase peak-position ratios can be consistent with 1 : √3 : 2 : √7, but the indexing,
number of reflections and competing phases matter. A hexagonal outline or a single image is
insufficient. Photocuring describes chemical network formation; crystallization describes structural
ordering. [M17,M18,M21]

log net D                                                                    MATERIAL RESPONSE AND MOTION




Biomechanics in physical coordinates
Geometry can influence response, but mechanical claims need their own measurements.




These continuum definitions relate displacement u, deformation gradient F and Green-Lagrange
strain E_G. For small deformations, ε ≈ ½(∇u + ∇uᵀ). The coordinate scale, camera projection and
displacement registration must be calibrated before a CCD image can support strain estimates.

 Quantity              Example definition or test                      Interpretation limit

 Stiffness             Force/displacement slope for a defined          Depends on specimen shape and
                       geometry.                                       supports.

 Modulus               Stress/strain response under a stated model.    Depends on loading regime and material
                                                                       state.

 Strength              Failure stress in a specified test.             Does not follow from stiffness alone.

 Toughness             Work to failure per volume, or an appropriate   State the definition and loading geometry.
                       fracture measure.

 Hardness              Resistance in a specified indentation method.   Not a general synonym for cured or stiff.



Suggested measurement sequence
Record specimen dimensions, hydration, temperature and conditioning time. Measure a mechanical
response before and after the selected cure/conditioning sequence. Include the carbohydrate
network alone, the lipid-containing material and any relevant interface control. Report replicates,
variability and failure location.

For dynamic loading, retain force/displacement timing and the acquisition phase between channels.
An analog multiplexer can introduce offsets that resemble phase lag; use actual sample times or
suitable simultaneous acquisition when the inference requires it. [M03]

Display deformation is not specimen deformation


A bounded radial map changes the apparent deformation gradient. Compute physical strain before
applying that display map, or reconstruct calibrated physical coordinates first. Swizzling a
displacement tuple also requires its component labels to follow the values.

Photopolymerization can involve oxygen inhibition and shrinkage. Their effects must be characterized
for the selected composition and geometry. Neither a lipid addition nor a honeycomb appearance
guarantees improved strength, toughness or biocompatibility. [M22,M23; Appendix A]

from the integer LUT decoder and the physical-unit record. Render the center at its declared coordinate

execution model from the canonical data packet.

explicitly draws the original and reflected set. Handle axis points once where duplicate brightness
matters. Inkblot resemblance is a visual motif; interpretation belongs to the named measurement or

Relative coordinates are a representation choice; the source text does not establish anonymity.




Origin removal and successive displacement encoding are different operations. With the initial

and anonymisation are distinct concepts. [M11]

laboratory-distance formulas. Reordering longitude and latitude is a field-layout operation, not a

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                                    CONCEPT AND SCOPE




BIOCHEMISTRY + BIOMECHANICS



Two-stage lipid-
carbohydrate preparation
Preparaat 1: lipids | Preparaat 2: carbohydrates
UV curing, hexagonal architecture and crystalline order

A plausible concept is to prepare defined lipid domains, incorporate them into a
photocurable carbohydrate-polymer formulation, and use light to fix a designed shape. Any
claim of internal hexagonal or crystalline order requires separate evidence. [1,2]


   STAGE 1                                            STAGE 2

   Preparaat 1                                        Preparaat 2 + light
   Defined lipid preparation                          Combine, shape and crosslink




                                                                             Carbohydrate network
                                                                             containing lipid domains




Schematic only. Colors identify phases; no size, dose or mechanical property is implied.



    Central distinction
    UV curing forms chemical bonds in a reactive formulation. A hexagonal mold defines geometry.
    Crystallization requires evidence of ordered structure. None of these observations substitutes
    for the others. [1,2]



Interpretation used in this report
Here, preparaat means a material preparation, and the two stages produce one composite. The main
proposal is a carbohydrate-derived network containing lipid domains. A separate lipid coating plus
carbohydrate coating is discussed as an alternative with its own adhesion problem.

No lipid identity, carbohydrate identity, resin, wavelength, specimen dimensions or intended
application was specified. The examples below explain possible chemistry; they do not constitute a
validated formulation or a prediction of performance.

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                                 BIOCHEMICAL MECHANISM




What each preparation contributes
Define the molecular role before choosing the curing system.


Preparaat 1 - lipids
Lipids are a broad family. Neutral oils can provide hydrophobic domains; amphiphilic lipids, with
polar and nonpolar regions, can form organized structures in water. The selected lipid, hydration
and environment determine the phase. A droplet dispersion and an inverse hexagonal lipid phase
are different starting materials. [6,7]

For the main proposed architecture, Stage 1 establishes the lipid identity, amount, domain size and
stability over the intended processing interval. Its role could be compartmentalization or a change
in mechanical response. These are design aims to test; lipid addition does not establish
reinforcement.

Preparaat 2 - carbohydrates
Choose a specific carbohydrate polymer and a defined reactive derivative. Methacrylated
hyaluronic acid (MeHA), for example, is a polysaccharide modified with polymerizable groups.
Published studies formed photocrosslinked HA networks and showed that polymer concentration
and degree of modification influence swelling and mechanical properties. [3,4]

In an aqueous formulation, light-induced network formation can produce a hydrogel: a polymer
network containing substantial water. A gel can retain its shape while remaining soft. Native sugar,
an unmodified polysaccharide and a photocurable derivative are therefore different formulation
choices. [1,3,4]

  Material choice                        Role and chemical limitation


  Native lipid domains                   May be physically trapped in the carbohydrate network. Covalent attachment
                                         is not established by entrapment.


  Reactive lipid-derived resin           Acrylated epoxidized soybean oil (AESO) is a documented photocurable
                                         example. Its chemical modification is essential to that example. It is not
                                         evidence that arbitrary oil will UV-harden. [5]


  Functionalized                         Can supply the continuous photocrosslinked phase when its reactive groups,
  polysaccharide                         initiator and illumination are compatible. MeHA is an example, not a selected
                                         recipe. [3,4]



The interface is part of the design
The proposed mixture must remain sufficiently uniform while it is shaped and cured. Test wetting,
coalescence, phase separation and lipid retention. Mixing may change hydration, ionic conditions or
the internal lipid phase; repeat structural measurements after incorporation and after curing. A
stable-looking specimen does not prove that the original nanostructure survived.

Alternative laminate: depositing a carbohydrate layer on a lipid layer requires a separately

preparations neither creates a glycolipid nor guarantees chemical bonds between the phases.

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                        STRUCTURE AND TERMINOLOGY




What does “hexagonal” mean?
Geometry, liquid-crystalline order and molecular crystals require different evidence.


  EXTERNAL SHAPE                                   LIPID MESOPHASE                   MOLECULAR ORDER




      A molded hexagonal object                         Cylindrical water channels      Illustrative hexagonal cell
       or a cellular honeycomb                            seen in cross-section       Actual lattice must be indexed



All drawings are conceptual and have independent scales. No measured crystal structure is shown.


1. A six-sided object or a honeycomb
A mold, mask, projector or printing path can impose a macroscopic or microscopic hexagonal
shape. A solid hexagonal prism is different from a honeycomb with open cells. Verify dimensions
and cell walls by calibrated imaging. The external outline alone says nothing about molecular
crystallinity. [2]

2. A hexagonal liquid-crystalline lipid phase
In an inverse hexagonal phase, HII, water channels are surrounded by lipid monolayers and
arranged on a two-dimensional hexagonal lattice. This is mesophase order. It does not by itself
establish a three-dimensional molecular crystal. Appropriate lipid chemistry and environmental
conditions are required. [2,6,7]

Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) can support phase identification through an indexed reflection
sequence. For an ideal two-dimensional hexagonal lattice, characteristic q-position ratios include 1
: √3 : 2 : √7. Several consistent peaks and a structural model are more informative than one peak
or optical texture. Compare before mixing, after mixing and after curing. [7]

3. A molecular crystal
A claim of crystalline phase identity needs suitable diffraction evidence, commonly wide-angle
X-ray scattering or X-ray diffraction (WAXS/XRD), with thermal analysis as support where
appropriate. A six-sided face does not identify the crystal system. [2]


    A real precedent, with a specific limitation
    Engineered reactive lipids have been crosslinked while retaining H order. The cited study used
                                                                           II
    redox initiation. It supports the possibility of fixing an appropriately designed mesophase, but
    does not validate a generic UV resin mixed with lipids and carbohydrates. [6]

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                         OPTICS AND THE SUPPLIED IMAGE




What the light diagram establishes
A Fresnel lens and a parabolic reflector are alternative collimating approaches.




Figure 1. User-supplied reference image, reproduced with its original credit: © Parabolix Lighting LLC,
www.parabolixlight.com. The illustration concerns ray direction; it provides no measured UV spectrum or irradiance.


Collimation controls direction
For an ideal point source at the relevant focal position, a Fresnel lens refracts light into a near-parallel
beam; a paraboloidal reflector performs the corresponding operation by reflection. Real source size
and alignment limit collimation. Lens transmission and mirror reflectance must suit the actual curing
wavelength. [8,10]

Uniform exposure is a separate requirement
Parallel rays do not guarantee equal irradiance over the specimen. Newport’s flood-exposure design,
for example, combines a homogenizer with a collimating lens. For this concept, measure the
illumination across the specimen plane with the actual window, optic and patterning arrangement
installed. [9]


    How this relates to a hexagon
    Use a defined mold or a validated exposure pattern to establish the external shape. The
    collimator itself supplies neither a hexagonal mold nor evidence of hexagonal molecular order.
    Select the source by spectral overlap with the photoinitiating chemistry, then calibrate the
    delivered exposure. [8-11]

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                          PHOTOCHEMISTRY AND EXPOSURE




How UV hardening would work
Network formation, cure depth and final mechanical properties are separate measurements.


A representative reaction mechanism
For a free-radical (meth)acrylate formulation, an appropriate photoinitiating system absorbs light
and generates reactive radicals. These react with polymerizable groups; sufficient intermolecular
linking produces a network. The carbohydrate backbone supplies the polymer scaffold in the MeHA
example. Other UV-resin chemistries can use different mechanisms. [1,3,5]


    Conceptual sequence
    Light absorption → reactive species → polymerization / crosslinking → network
    formation
    For the proposed aqueous carbohydrate route, the product may remain a hydrated gel.
    Hardness, stiffness and crystallinity must each be established separately.



Quantify the exposure at the specimen

  Quantity                              Expression and interpretation


  Radiant exposure H                    H(x,y) = ∫ I(x,y,t) dt
                                        For constant irradiance, H = I × t. With I in mW/cm² and t in seconds, H is in
                                        mJ/cm². Record the spectrum as well as the energy. [11]


  Calibrated cure-depth                 Cd = Dp ln(H / Hc), for H > Hc
  model                                 Cd: gelled depth; Dp: fitted optical penetration parameter; Hc: fitted gelation
                                        threshold. This is an empirical working-curve approximation within its
                                        validated range. [11]


  Conversion α                          α=1-R          /R
                                                 after    before
                                        R can be a reactive-group spectral signal normalized to a stable reference.
                                        The chosen band, baseline and depth sampling must be appropriate to the
                                        chemistry. [5,12,13]


Illustrative arithmetic only: 5 mW/cm² for 20 s gives 100 mJ/cm² at the measured plane. This is not
a recommended curing dose. Equal total exposure at different irradiances need not give equal
conversion, and none of these numbers specifies the energy reaching the specimen interior. [11]

Why a solid-looking surface is insufficient
Cure depth identifies a gelled layer; it does not alone determine conversion or stiffness. Oxygen can
inhibit free-radical polymerization near an exposed surface, while reaction kinetics and optical
attenuation can produce depth-dependent curing. Lipid domains may change scattering or phase
partitioning, so the complete mixture needs its own measurements. [11-13]

Record dimensional change and temperature as well as conversion. Acrylate polymerization can

hypotheses to examine. A rigid dry object requires a specifically designed formulation and drying or

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                           BIOMECHANICAL INTERPRETATION




How the composite may carry load
The following effects are testable hypotheses, not measured performance claims.

Biomechanics here concerns how the bio-derived composite deforms, relaxes and fails under
controlled loading. Hydration and test conditions are part of the material description.

 Property                              Meaning for this material

 Stiffness / modulus                   Resistance to deformation at a stated strain range. Greater stiffness does not
                                       automatically mean greater strength or toughness.

 Strength                              Stress associated with a defined failure or yielding criterion. Report the failure
                                       mode, not only the maximum force.

 Toughness / energy                    Energy needed for fracture, or energy absorbed during a defined loading path.
 absorption                            These require a specified test and are not interchangeable.

 Hardness                              Resistance to localized indentation under a stated method. A shape-stable gel
                                       need not be hard.


Constituents, interfaces and architecture
Carbohydrate network. Polymer identity, concentration, reactive-group density, conversion and
hydration help determine mechanical response. HA studies demonstrate that formulation changes
alter swelling and moduli, but their numerical results cannot be transferred to this unspecified
composite. [3,4]

Lipid domains. Soft inclusions could lower an effective modulus or alter energy dissipation. Solid
lipid domains could behave differently. Poorly coupled domains could act as defects. Domain size,
lipid state and interfacial bonding determine which explanation is consistent with the
measurements; lipid content alone is insufficient.

Hexagonal architecture. For a honeycomb, wall thickness, cell size, relative density, vertices,
defects and loading direction matter. A published polymer-honeycomb study found that changing
vertex architecture changed deformation and mechanical performance. This supports testing the
actual geometry; it does not supply a strength prediction for the proposed chemistry. [15]

Report mechanics in the state of intended use
Specify hydration medium, conditioning time, temperature, specimen dimensions and loading rate.
Include relaxation or cyclic loading if time dependence matters. Test after conditioning as well as
after fabrication, so swelling or lipid loss is not hidden by a dry-only result.


    Minimal compression quantities
    σ = F / A0 ε = Δh / h0 Eapp = Δσ / Δε
    Use a stated compression-positive convention and strain interval. F is force, A0 the chosen initial
    area, h0 initial height and Δh shortening. Gross-area stress for a honeycomb yields an effective

LIPIDS / CARBOHYDRATES / UV                                                                       RESEARCH PLAN




A two-stage validation sequence
Move from an explicitly defined formulation to claims supported by measurements.


Stage 1 - establish Preparaat 1
Specify the lipid and its role; prepare a reproducible dispersion or selected self-assembled phase.
Record composition, domain size, hydration and temperature. For an HII claim, collect phase evidence
before incorporation. Retain this material as a reference.

Stage 2 - combine, shape and cure Preparaat 2
Specify the carbohydrate derivative and photoinitiating system. Establish compatibility with Preparaat
1, impose the chosen geometry, calibrate exposure on small specimens of known thickness, and
measure conversion and properties after curing. Repeat phase and dimensional checks after the
intended conditioning step.

 Question                      Measurement to plan                              Claim it supports

 Did a network form?           Reaction-specific FTIR/NIR, rheology and an      Chemical conversion and network
                               appropriate gel / extractables assessment.       development, separately from
                                                                                appearance. [5,12,13]

 Is cure adequate              Irradiance map, thickness series, and            A process window for the actual resin,
 throughout?                   accessible surface / interior conversion         optics and specimen. [11,12]
                               checks.

 Are lipids retained?          Domain imaging and a validated                   Distribution and retention; not
                               lipid-retention or mass-balance                  automatically chemical bonding.
                               measurement.

 Is hexagonal order            Dimensional imaging for shape; SAXS for          The specific scale and kind of order
 present?                      mesophase; WAXS/XRD for crystal phase.           measured. [2,7]

 Is the structure              Compression or tension, relaxation / cycles as   Mechanical behavior under the
 useful?                       relevant, and failure imaging.                   reported test conditions.



Controls that separate the possible causes
Use the carbohydrate network without lipid; the combined formulation without exposure; Preparaat 1
before incorporation; and a geometry comparison under an explicit mass or dimension constraint.
Compare independent preparation batches. Match non-lipid ingredients where possible and measure
conversion, rather than assuming it is equal.


    Information needed for an executable protocol
    Exact lipid and carbohydrate identities; chemical modification; water or solvent content; resin and
    initiator; intended lipid fraction; specimen thickness and hexagon scale; source spectrum;

photocured hexagonal architecture.” Add “hexagonal liquid-crystalline lipid phase” or “crystalline” only
when the relevant structural evidence supports that additional statement.

# TOM World & Query Kernel 0.6.0

TOMK is a research implementation of a deterministic finite symbolic learner and its publication pipeline. Kernel 0.6.0 / TOM Learner 0.2 evaluates 121 literal hypotheses from four exact families against sixteen supplied data sets. It records ambiguity, counterexamples, contradiction and regression evidence, then materializes accepted or rejected outcomes through the TOMAGI runtime shipped in this repository.

The Hugging Face repository is [c0mbatduckzz/TOMK](https://huggingface.co/c0mbatduckzz/TOMK). Start with the [learner specification](spec/TOM_LEARNER_0_2_WORLD_QUERY_KERNEL_0_6.md), [seeded compiler specification](spec/TOM_SEEDED_COMPILATION_1_0.md), and [formal language specification](spec/TOM_FORMAL_LANGUAGE_1_0.md). The code and literal definitions are released under the [MIT license](LICENSE).

The exact authoritative seed is [TOM_seed_genome_2026-09-01.txt](TOM_seed_genome_2026-09-01.txt): 244 ASCII bytes, no terminal newline, SHA-256 `d1417a3136772c0cf3eddcd4962ce07d42cbf87616f7b5bae09fc652d9b807b5`. Its requester-supplied attribution is Tom Klootwijk; [personal field omitted]; [personal field omitted], as recorded in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). The identifiers are supplied attribution and were not independently verified.

## TOM Learner 0.2 — finite typed hypothesis-family authority

WQK 0.6 continues the corrected authority roadmap rather than restarting it. The exact canonical TOM seed remains the root. The fixed TOMAGI 1.0 ABI remains 128-byte header, 64-byte `State64`, 48-byte `Cell48`, and sixteen opcodes.

The release incorporates and regression-tests the CODEX 0.5.2 kernel repairs before broadening the learner:

- defined C arithmetic with explicit `wrap32` lowering;
- rejection of all nonzero reserved TOMAGI header words in Python and C;
- same-host thread/process publication locking from expected-HEAD read through atomic replacement;
- recursive formal-value and canonical-byte limits at every intermediate node;
- reproducible package construction from pinned authority sources; and
- public `audit-store SOURCE STORE` argument order.

Above that repaired boundary, WQK 0.6 implements a finite content-addressed registry of four exact hypothesis families:

| Family | Candidates |
|---|---:|
| Rational polynomial, degree at most two | 34 |
| One-breakpoint piecewise affine | 21 |
| Complete finite transition table | 27 |
| Depth-two expression tree | 39 |
| **Total** | **121** |

The domain decision is made by static content-addressed formal definitions. The generic Python formal evaluator evaluates the declared learner and promotion operations during seeded compilation. The compiler canonically encodes those results and lowers them into a `Cell48` graph that emits the result bytes. Python and C then execute the compiled `.tmg` program; authenticated ordered `EMIT` records reproduce the materialized bytes. This release's learner search therefore runs at compilation time, while TOMAGI execution replays its compiled output.

Host Python also provides strict validation, independent falsification, trace authentication and generic immutable storage. The separately implemented `fractions.Fraction` oracle compares the learner outcomes and cannot select or publish an authoritative result.

## Authority chain

```text
canonical 244-byte TOM seed + pinned literal definitions and exact data sets
-> verified content-addressed dependency graph
-> bounded formal learner and promotion evaluation during compilation
-> canonical result bytes
-> deterministic Cell48 EMIT lowering and compiled .tmg
-> equal Python/C TOMAGI execution
-> replay-authenticated EMIT materialization
-> same-host locked immutable publication
-> reconstructed terminal HEAD
```

Multiple exact train survivors produce an explicit ambiguity record and rejection. There is no hidden stable-sort winner. Supersession proposals must pass regression cases for all pinned prior definitions. Accepted and rejected sessions both continue through the parent-bound 0.5.2 publication profile.

The installed entry points expose the Python runtime and CLI. Keep the repository checkout available for the seed, formal programs, fixtures, C sources and Make recipes. The [publication manifest](examples/publication/documents.json) and [document validation](validation/publication/validation_report.json) additionally bind twelve publication documents, including both use-case reports in PDF and Markdown, to executable literal definitions. Each document is compiled and checked through equal Python/C traces, ordered `EMIT` records and exact materialized bytes. For the imported reports this proves archival replay. Their proposed applications remain proposals. The full source, generated programs, traces and inventories are available in the [complete release archive](releases/TOM_World_Query_Kernel_0_6_0_Tom_Klootwijk.zip); its [external audit](releases/TOM_World_Query_Kernel_0_6_EXTERNAL_ARCHIVE_AUDIT.json) records complete ZIP equality across two independent builds and a finished-archive replay.

Preserve the complete archive and its matching manifests for reproduction. A mathematical determinism argument in the specifications and the recorded conformance tests are different forms of evidence; this release provides no machine-checked proof of the whole implementation.

## Proposed use cases

The supplied use-case documents describe application architectures and proposed future development. Their implementation status is **proposal**: the designs extend beyond the implemented and validated capabilities of kernel 0.6.0. The kernel's current evidence remains the finite four-family learner, deterministic compilation and execution, and authenticated publication pipeline described above.

## Evidence boundary

This release demonstrates exact finite search over four literal hypothesis families. It does not establish noisy learning, open-domain induction, cognitive memory, planning, perception, autonomous action, distributed consensus, physical GPU execution, general intelligence, or AGI.

The next milestone is **TOM Learner 0.3 / WQK 0.7**: interval-valued observations and finite noise families with explicit calibration, coverage, distribution-shift, ambiguity, supersession, and regression evidence. Confidence must remain a typed record rather than an invisible TOMAGI control path.

# Maktub — a self-rewriting state model

**Paradigm author: Tom Klootwijk / [personal field omitted] / [personal field omitted]**

![Tom Klootwijk — paraaf](assets/tom-klootwijk-paraaf.png)

Maktub is an executable study of rules that participate in the systems they govern. Every event produces both a successor state and the description of the next rule:

$$
x_{n+1}=\operatorname{Act}(x_n,d_n,e_n),\qquad
d_{n+1}=\operatorname{Rewrite}(x_n,d_n,e_n).
$$

Both updates read the **same pre-transition configuration**. The rule description is explicit, changing data, so the trace records how the system acts and how its future behavior is rewritten. This is the operational core of the source paradigm's **Universal State Bookkeeping**.

This release provides a **symbolic model with custom Python code**: a deterministic reference kernel, configuration, runnable examples, tests, and source provenance. Its equations run directly, with every transition available for inspection. “Self-rewriting” means updating the represented operator description.

## Run the model

Download the [model repository](https://huggingface.co/c0mbatduckzz/Maktub-Tom-Klootwijk), or clone it:

```bash
git clone https://huggingface.co/c0mbatduckzz/Maktub-Tom-Klootwijk
cd Maktub-Tom-Klootwijk
```

From that directory:

```python
from maktub_kernel import MaktubKernel

model = MaktubKernel.from_pretrained(".")
record = model.step(state=0, description=0, event=None)
print(record["next"])
# {'state': 1, 'description': 1}

trace = model.run([None, None, None], state=0, description=0)
print([entry["next"]["state"] for entry in trace])
# [1, 0, 1]
```

The default **one-bit mirror** profile implements the formal specification's exact reduction: $x_n=d_n=b_n\in\{0,1\}$, with both outputs equal to $1-b_n$. The transition record also preserves the supplied event.

An optional **adaptive boundary** profile makes the paired architecture visible in a larger state:

```python
boundary = MaktubKernel.from_pretrained(".", profile="adaptive_boundary")
record = boundary.step(
    state={"accepted": 0, "released": 0},
    description={"threshold": 0.5, "learning_rate": 0.1},
    event=0.8,
)
print(record)
```

Admission uses the old threshold; the same event then moves the next threshold toward itself. The formula $\tau'=\tau+\lambda(e-\tau)$ is a **new demonstration choice in this release**, instantiating the paired architecture with explicit adaptive dynamics.

## Geometry and form

The kernel also exposes the source-derived log-polar and JSF/JDS form model. It keeps spatial radius, logarithmic quantity, angle, and mixing weight separate:

$$
\rho=\ln(r/r_{\mathrm{ref}}),\quad\theta=\operatorname{atan2}(y,x),\quad
\alpha(n)=\operatorname{clip}\!\left(\frac{9-\log_{10}n}{4},0,1\right).
$$

cards.title: Maktub-Tom-Klootwijk pinned README, chunk 2
cards.text:
The two named fields are combined as $F_{\mathrm{mix}}=(1-\alpha)F_{\mathrm{JSF}}+\alpha F_{\mathrm{JDS}}$. In the published example, JSF is a circle and JDS has a selected sinusoidal boundary perturbation. Their parameters are the educational synthesis's chosen model values.

```python
from math import cos, pi, sin

theta = pi / 16
result = model.predict(x=cos(theta), y=sin(theta), quantity=10**7)
print(round(result["mixed_field"], 2), result["location"])
# 0.06 outside
```

Here the analytic mixed field is approximately `0.06`, locating the point outside the chosen contour. `predict` returns the analytic fields, mixing weight, weighted contributions, and location. The output explicitly identifies its field type.

## Grounding and verification

| Layer | What this release establishes |
|---|---|
| Source paradigm | A documented paired state/operator transition, one-bit mirror, boundary vocabulary, and domain correspondences. |
| Operational model | Explicit Python rules, typed inputs, deterministic traces, log-polar conversions, and analytic field calculations. |
| Verification | Reproducible checks of the implemented algebra, input contracts, and transition behavior. |

The six supplied PDFs preserve both Tom Klootwijk's prompts and the assistant responses that helped elaborate the paradigm. The later formal and educational documents distinguish definitions, numerical equality, and analogy. This release carries that provenance into explicit executable profiles and a documented source-to-code map.

Read the [conceptual context](docs/context.md), [source lineage and attribution](docs/provenance.md), and [SHA-256 source manifest](provenance.json) for page-level grounding, original PDFs, and the distinction between retained equations and new implementation choices.

**Intended use:** inspectable symbolic computation, state-machine research prototypes, reproducible demonstrations, and teaching model construction. The kernel implements the one-bit mirror, adaptive-boundary demonstration, log-polar transforms, Hadamard operations, and JSF/JDS analytic field model.

# TOM-MAKTUBIII

**Formalism author: Tom Klootwijk. Version 3.0.0. Released 10 October 2026.**

TOM-MAKTUBIII is an executable symbolic model of the paired state-and-rule architecture in *Maktub III: Signature-field kinematic calculus*. It provides primitive shell-operator inputs, signed fields, Hadamard composition, Klein-chart adapters, dual-pin Fourier routing, log-time coordinates, 25-site addressing, and a time-indexed Power Paper T transaction record.

Every transition computes both successors from the same pre-event snapshot:

$$
x_{n+1}=\operatorname{Act}(x_n,d_n,e_n),\qquad
d_{n+1}=\operatorname{Rewrite}(x_n,d_n,e_n).
$$

The current description selects the current gates. A requested rewrite becomes active on the next event. The finalized readout includes both the applied and next descriptions, connected to the successor state through an acyclic record ID.

This release is a custom Python research model with explicit numerical rules. It has no learned weights, training dataset, or training run, and is loaded through `MaktubIII`, rather than a Transformers text-generation pipeline. The original PDFs are included unchanged with SHA-256 provenance.

## Run

Python 3.10 or later; the numerical model uses only the standard library.

```bash
git clone https://huggingface.co/c0mbatduckzz/TOM-MAKTUBIII
cd TOM-MAKTUBIII
python -m pip install -e .
python examples/run_demo.py
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

```python
from maktubiii import MaktubIII

model = MaktubIII.from_pretrained(".")
event = {
    "T": 1.0,
    "point": [2.0, 0.0],
    "fields": [0.2, -0.4],
    "samples": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0],
    "rewrite": {"alpha": 1.0, "gate2": [1.0, 1.0]},
}
record = model.step(event)
print(record["next"]["state"]["last_result"])
# approximately -0.05; this event used the old alpha=0.5
```

After installing the source package, optional remote configuration loading is available:

```bash
python -m pip install "huggingface_hub>=0.25"
```

```python
model = MaktubIII.from_pretrained("c0mbatduckzz/TOM-MAKTUBIII")
# Pass revision="<commit SHA>" to pin a published configuration.
```

## Shell operators are primitive inputs

A shell operator can define its own field behavior. The interface records its carrier, metric, units, representation and identity; `evaluate(point, time)` supplies the value. Signed-distance samplers and signed-form samplers can both participate. User-defined primitives do not need to reduce to the supplied circle example.

```python
from shell_operators import CircleShell, PrimitiveShell

shell_a = CircleShell(radius=1.0)
shell_b = CircleShell(radius=1.5)
product = shell_a.hadamard(shell_b)
print(product.evaluate((2.0, 0.0)))  # 1.0 * 0.5 = 0.5

cards.title: TOM-MAKTUBIII pinned README, chunk 2
cards.text:
# A user-defined shell sampler is a first-class input:
custom = PrimitiveShell(
    name="my-shell",
    sampler=lambda point, time: (point[0]**2 + point[1]**2)**0.5 - 1.0,
    carrier="euclidean", metric="euclidean", units="length",
    representation="signed_distance", dimension=2,
)

shell_event = {"T": 1.0, "point": [2.0, 0.0], "samples": [1, 2, 3, 4]}
record = model.step(shell_event, shell_pair=(custom, shell_b))
```

`shell_pair` is supplied at inference time. Its values and operator specifications enter the trace; arbitrary Python sampler code is not serialized into `config.json`. `KleinPullback` accepts a supplied coordinate map, and `check_klein_seams` checks the two quotient seam relations on a declared sample grid. A shell can use a Klein carrier directly. See [the shell example](examples/shell_demo.py).

The exact Euclidean disk example has a known signed-distance interpretation. A custom sampler's distance label is a declared contract. Products and general coordinate pullbacks return signed form fields because neither operation universally preserves distance. Shell composition is operational; physical realization depends on the supplied material interpretation and evidence.

## Validation outcome

The formalism is **partially validated as mathematics and an executable record architecture**. See the [full validation report](docs/VALIDATION.md), [equation-to-code map](docs/equation-map.json), and [reproducible evaluation](evaluation/results.json).

The release reproduces the page 23 example: local key **11**, binary search path **12 → 5 → 8 → 10 → 11**, gated channels **(0.1, −0.15)**, and mixed output **−0.05**. It also implements the time chain rule, normalized Hadamard transform, forward DFT, inverse butterfly, inverse DFT, and full retained-sample reconstruction. Fourier reference routines use direct subtransforms and cost O(N²); they expose the algebra rather than provide a high-performance FFT.

The paired transaction is a concrete reference profile: supplied LUT row/column labels identify a computed entry; an explicit event rewrite sets next-event gate parameters; the root support contains 25 sites. Recursive L-system growth, full Klein transport, a constitutive shoelepel mechanics model, and the H.7/H.9 boundary-integral interpretation need further supplied operators or definitions. Signature metadata is associated with fields as a typed record, without multiplying name/date strings as numbers.

The pea-soup conversation contains a valid inverse-butterfly formula and assertions about material reconstruction. The code demonstrates recovery of **retained numerical samples**. Changing a time encoding, recovering Fourier coefficients, or computing a zero interface does not by itself establish a process that turns cooked soup into whole peas. Such a claim remains unvalidated by these documents; the model accepts future physical shell interpretations as explicit inputs.

| --- | --- | --- |

| Twin coordinate representation | Cartesian position is encoded by signed logarithms followed by canonical polar coordinates, with a specified inverse. | Compact C.2, p.2 |
| Evolution and fourth product | Transport the chosen transition through the chart and retain both before/after views in one ordered record. | Compact C.4, p.3; C.10, p.6 |

## Core equations available directly as text

cards.title: JTK-Twin-Viper pinned README, chunk 3
cards.text:
The signed-log-polar chart uses positive lengths `ell` and `H`, and a declared `z0`:

```text
slog(x) = sign(x) * ln(1 + abs(x)/ell)
u = slog(x);  v = slog(y);  zeta = (z-z0)/H
R = sqrt(u*u + v*v)
theta = atan2(v,u) mod (2*pi);  R=0 => theta=0
W(x,y,z) = (R,theta,zeta)
slog_inverse(u) = ell * sign(u) * (exp(abs(u))-1)
```

Here `R` is chart radius. The energy remainder below is written `E_remainder` to
keep its meaning distinct. For a chosen Cartesian transition `F_i`:

```text
F_i_chart = W compose F_i compose W_inverse
Q_i(x) = (x, W(x), F_i(x), W(F_i(x)))
corner_rank(k,a,b) = 4*k + 2*a + b;  a,b in {0,1}
```

The source energy profile is:

```text
epsilon = exp(-alpha/G)
E_reference = m*c*c
E_g = epsilon * E_reference
E_remainder = (1-epsilon) * E_reference
Y0(E_g,E_remainder) = (E_reference,E_g)
```

Use `m>0`, `G>0`, and `alpha>=0`; `alpha/G` is dimensionless. In the supplied
profiles `G` and `alpha` are dimensionless. Compute the physical gradient norm
with its declared metric and field normalization. For a differentiable true
signed-distance field in that metric, `G=1`. The `Y0` outputs are overlapping
total/allocated readouts; summing them would double-count the allocation.

## Apply it now

With Python 3.10 or later and the repository files downloaded:

```bash
python runtime/jtk_reference.py --input runtime/example_input.json --output result.json
python -m unittest discover -s runtime -p "test_*.py" -v
```

The [input example](runtime/example_input.json) declares a quarter-turn profile
from `(1,0,0)` metres with `ell=H=1 m`. Its successor is approximately `(0,1,0)`
and the fourth corner is `(ln(2), pi/2, 0)` in the chart. The program reports
the discrepancy between direct and transported chart evolution.

The example also evaluates independent energy, rational-LUT, and oscillator
blocks. With `m=1e-9 kg`, `alpha=ln(2)`, `G=1`, and `c=299792458 m/s`, it gives:

```text
epsilon = 0.5
E_reference = 89875517.87368177 J
E_g = E_remainder = 44937758.936840884 J
```

See the [complete output](runtime/example_output.json). Change the JSON inputs
for another declared profile, or implement a new `F_i` and transport it through
the same chart. The guide maps each function to its equations and input units.

## Formalization and implemented behavior

TK-SROF defines a family of typed operator-bearing transition systems. A selected operator acts on the committed old snapshot; a validated rewrite changes descriptions used by later execution. TK-EDGE-1 implements the exact finite pinion profile, typed role/gene changes, a finite U-TAPE-1 interpreter, checkpoints, fixed-member peer replay and CUDA disk-backed state paging.
